meaning: reviewed declarative/statement clitic plus clause-connecting conjunction -na ('and')

note: This first stage recognizes wuuna/wayna/waana only as the first lexical token of an overt second clause. Standalone or internally attached uses remain unjudged.

rule: The subject person encoded by wuuna/wayna may be checked only against an exact reviewed finite verb in a short local predicate window. No antecedent or unseen verb form is inferred.

wuuna/wayna/waana are statement/declarative constructions and remain distinct from connective focus buuna/beyna and subject-focus ayaana/baana. No broader waa+subject-clitic+-na paradigm is generated.

waana = waa + connective -na. Because the exact form contains no short subject pronoun, it is recognized as a person-neutral connective declarative particle and does not license a subject-person or finite-agreement judgment by itself.

When the nearest preceding reviewed statement subject clitic is wuu, way, or waad, compare its reviewed person set with the exact right connective statement clitic in wuuna/wayna. If the sets overlap, same-subject continuation is compatible. If they are disjoint, mark subject continuity context-required rather than a grammatical agreement error: -na links two clauses, so a different discourse subject may be intended. Do not infer antecedent identity or autofix the connective.
